webui.description: Browser UI served by `nanopi webui` (packages/webui, copied to dist/webui and embedded in single-file builds)

export-html.description: HTML export templates and vendored assets (dist/core/export-html)

docs.description: In-package documentation (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships it)

examples.description: In-package examples (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships them)

tools.description: Built-in tool set the build registers, as a group key over the per-tool components: every "tools/<name>" was a switch in older configs and is derived from the flavor's tool set instead

tools/read.description: The read tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/bash.description: The bash tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/powershell.description: The powershell tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/edit.description: The edit tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/write.description: The write tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/grep.description: The grep tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/find.description: The find tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/ls.description: The ls tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

embedded-code.description: Embedded-code detection for shell call display (heredoc bodies and interpreter inline scripts); dropping it renders shell commands as one block

jiti-modules.description: Loading module files from disk with jiti: .nanopi/extensions/, the agent directory's extensions/, and $NANOPI_EXTENSIONS. Dropping it takes jiti out of the build, which leaves only the compiled-in modules (the single-file build never loads disk modules either way)

syntax-highlight.description: highlight.js grammars and the code highlighting the TUI uses; dropping it renders code blocks in the plain output color and takes ~1.4 MiB of grammars out of the bundle

goal.description: Goal tracking module (planned; registered so its build wiring lands with the module)

toolset.description: Built-in tool set the build registers: "standard" (read, bash, edit, write plus the optional tools) or "bash" (the shell tools alone). Flavors set it as a name, not a switch; group keys like "module/*" work here too

providers.description: Provider set the build registers: one entry from the top-level "providerSets" map. The build's model catalogs are generated for that set only, so a trimmed build carries no code or data for the providers it drops. Flavors set it as a name, not a switch

apis.description: API implementations the build registers: one entry from the top-level "apiSets" map. A trimmed build ships no client for the APIs it drops, so models.json can only name the APIs its set carries. Flavors set it as a name, not a switch

module/extra.description: Run-mode, permission, and webui bridge module (packages/extra, @nanopi/pi-extra); a flavor that drops it aliases the module to an inert stub

module/codex-compaction.description: Codex-style compaction and its post-compaction warning

module/websearch.description: web_search and read_page tools with the keyless engine chain

sidecar/tui-native.description: TUI native prebuilds builtin in single-file builds (all platforms embedded; the matching one installs to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand)

sidecar/photon-wasm.description: photon wasm builtin in single-file builds (installed to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand)

full.description: Everything included; the only flavor the npm packages are published from

base.description: Core CLI with the standard tool set (read, edit, write, bash), a curated model catalog (openai, google, anthropic, glm/z.ai, qwen, kimi), every API implementation, and the HTML export templates; none of the bundled extras, docs, examples, the browser UI, sidecars or OAuth flows, so a login that needs a flow has to use an API key. Any other vendor is one `models.json` entry away

minimal.description: base with the bash tool alone, one endpoint shape, and no peripheral code: the shell tool is the only tool the build registers (the other tool definitions are stubbed out), endpoint API implementations are cut to openai-completions, the syntax-highlight grammars and embedded-code detection are dropped, run modes and permissions (module/extra) fall away with the extras, and the endpoint and key come from models.json instead of a shipped catalog

all.description: Every API implementation in packages/ai. The marker is checked against the registered API ids at build time, and the runtime registers everything it ships

openai.description: The OpenAI-compatible chat completions API alone: the smallest build talks to one endpoint shape, which is everything models.json needs to point at a local or self-hosted server

all.description: Every built-in provider catalog in packages/ai. The marker is checked against the generated catalogs at build time, and the model generator writes the concrete list back here once it writes more than one catalog, so a build never ships a provider the catalog does not have

core.description: The vendors a trimmed CLI keeps in its model picker: the assistants people reach for first (openai, google, anthropic, glm/z.ai, qwen, kimi). Every other catalog stays a one-entry `models.json` away but ships no data, which is where ~1.5 MiB of the bundle goes. `base` ships this set; `full` ships `all`

none.description: No built-in provider at all: the model generator writes an empty catalog, the runtime registers no built-in provider, and the endpoint and key come from models.json. This is the minimal SKU, which is why the set is a value and not a switch

presets.description: The preset providers a standard deployment configures: one catalog per vendor the CLI can talk to out of the box. The full set has the same members today; the two part ways as soon as the catalog grows an internal or stand-in provider
